titleEn: Changing the rules of a sports club
titleTh: ปรับกฎการเข้าซ้อมของชมรมกีฬา
scenarioSentences: You are the captain of your school's basketball club.
Many members have been missing training.
The team lost its last three games.
Coach Murray wants stricter rules.
You meet him to discuss it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Coach Murray, you wanted to talk about attendance?

dialogue.speaker: Coach Murray
dialogue.text: Yes. Half the team missed practice last week. If you miss two sessions, you shouldn't play on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That seems fair most of the time. But exams start next month, and people need to study.

dialogue.speaker: Coach Murray
dialogue.text: I understand, but otherwise we'll keep losing.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: What if the rule didn't apply during exam weeks, as long as players tell you in advance?

dialogue.speaker: Coach Murray
dialogue.text: That's reasonable. But they'd need to come to at least one session a week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I think everyone could manage that. Should we put it in writing?

dialogue.speaker: Coach Murray
dialogue.text: Yes. Could you write the new rules and share them with the team by Friday?

titleTh: ตั้งกฎการใช้โทรศัพท์ให้น้องชาย
scenarioSentences: Your brother Max is ten.
He spends hours on his phone every evening.
His teacher says he seems tired in class.
Dad wants to take the phone away completely.
You think that is too strict.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Dad, are you really going to take Max's phone away?

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: I'm thinking about it. He's on it until midnight and exhausted in class.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I know, but his friends all message each other. He'd feel left out.

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: So what would you suggest?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: What if he could use it after homework, but not after nine?

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: And hands the phone to me at nine? Otherwise, he'll use it in bed.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Exactly. It's also worth getting him into a sport, so he's busy after school.

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: He did enjoy soccer last year. I'll sign him up for the Saturday club.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good. Let's tell him together tonight, so it doesn't feel like a punishment.

dialogue.speaker: Dad
dialogue.text: Agreed. After dinner, then.

titleEn: Reporting a safety hazard at work
titleTh: แจ้งหัวหน้าเรื่องจุดอันตรายในที่ทำงาน
scenarioSentences: You work at a garden center.
A step on the storeroom stairs is broken.
You nearly fell this morning.
Mr. Lowe is your supervisor.
You go to tell him about it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Lowe, a step on the storeroom stairs is broken. I nearly fell.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lowe
dialogue.text: Are you hurt?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm fine. It's the third step from the top, and the wood's cracked through.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lowe
dialogue.text: That must have happened during the last delivery. We'll need it fixed.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Should we close the storeroom until then? Someone could get badly hurt.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lowe
dialogue.text: Not all week. We need stock for the weekend sale.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then let's close it today and move the sale items to the back office.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lowe
dialogue.text: Good idea. I'll call a repair company, and it should be fixed by Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll put a warning sign on the door.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lowe
dialogue.text: Thanks. Please write a short report too, so we have a record.

titleEn: Hiring a photographer for an event
titleTh: ต่อราคาจ้างช่างภาพงานชมรม
scenarioSentences: Your student club is holding an awards night.
You want a professional photographer.
Ms. Rhodes charges six hundred dollars.
Your club only has four hundred.
You call her to discuss the price.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Rhodes, we love your work, but six hundred is over our budget.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rhodes
dialogue.text: I understand. What's the most your club can spend?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Four hundred, I'm afraid. We have no sponsors.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rhodes
dialogue.text: My price covers four hours. Do you need me for the whole evening?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not really. The important part is the awards, from seven to nine.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rhodes
dialogue.text: Then I could do two hours for four hundred and fifty.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could you do four hundred if we let you use the photos on your website?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rhodes
dialogue.text: That's a fair deal. Four hundred, as long as my name appears with them.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Of course. Could you send the contract this week?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rhodes
dialogue.text: Sure, I'll email it tomorrow.

titleEn: Taking a job further from home
titleTh: ตัดสินใจรับงานที่ไกลบ้าน
scenarioSentences: You have been offered a new job.
It pays much better than your current one.
However, the office is ninety minutes away.
Your friend Isaac changed jobs last year.
You ask him what he thinks.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Isaac, I got the job offer! The pay's twenty percent higher.

dialogue.speaker: Isaac
dialogue.text: Congratulations! So why do you look worried?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The office is ninety minutes away. That's three hours a day on the train.

dialogue.speaker: Isaac
dialogue.text: That's a lot. I did a long commute for a year, and it wore me out.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So you'd turn it down?

dialogue.speaker: Isaac
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. Would they let you work from home some days?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: They didn't mention it. I could ask, I suppose.

dialogue.speaker: Isaac
dialogue.text: You should. If you could start later and avoid the rush hour, it'd be easier.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True. I'll accept, as long as they agree to flexible hours.

dialogue.speaker: Isaac
dialogue.text: Good plan. Ask them before you sign the contract.

titleEn: Explaining a delayed project to a client
titleTh: แจ้งลูกค้าว่างานเว็บไซต์จะเสร็จช้า
scenarioSentences: You run a small web design business.
Mr. Fleming's new website is due on Friday.
Your only developer has been ill all week.
The site will be a week late.
You call him to explain.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Fleming, I'm afraid your website won't be ready by Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fleming
dialogue.text: What? I've already told customers it launches next week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm really sorry. Our developer has been ill, and we need about one more week.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fleming
dialogue.text: That's a problem. I've paid for ads that start on Monday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could you move the ads? Otherwise, we could put up a simple home page first.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fleming
dialogue.text: I'll ask about the ads. But I expect something for the delay.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fair. We'll add the extra menu page you wanted at no cost.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fleming
dialogue.text: All right. So what's the new date?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Friday the 20th, and I'll send you progress updates every two days.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fleming
dialogue.text: Fine. As long as it's not late again.

titleEn: Choosing a venue for a class reunion
titleTh: เลือกสถานที่จัดงานเลี้ยงรุ่น
scenarioSentences: It has been ten years since you left school.
You and Paula are organizing a class reunion.
About sixty people plan to come.
You must book a venue soon.
You meet Paula to decide.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So, the school hall or the restaurant? We need to book this week.

dialogue.speaker: Paula
dialogue.text: I'd prefer the restaurant. The food's great, and nobody has to cook.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True, but they charge fifty dollars per person, and the room only fits forty.

dialogue.speaker: Paula
dialogue.text: Forty? That's not enough for everyone.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The hall holds over a hundred, and it's only two hundred dollars for the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Paula
dialogue.text: But who'd do the food? I'd rather not spend all night in the kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We could hire a food truck. It'd still be much cheaper.

dialogue.speaker: Paula
dialogue.text: And people would love being back in the old hall. Okay, you've convinced me.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. I'll call the school tomorrow to check the date.

titleEn: Deciding whether to report a cheating classmate
titleTh: ตัดสินใจว่าจะรายงานเพื่อนที่ลอกข้อสอบไหม
scenarioSentences: You had a math test today.
You and Jonah saw a classmate copying answers.
He had notes under his desk.
The test counts toward final grades.
You discuss it with Jonah at lunch.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Jonah, what should we do about Ryan? I'm sure he was copying.

dialogue.speaker: Jonah
dialogue.text: Me too. But if we tell Ms. Grant, he could fail the whole course.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's his fault, though. It's not fair to everyone who studied.

dialogue.speaker: Jonah
dialogue.text: I agree, but we might have misunderstood. What if it was just scrap paper?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I saw him reading from it. It was definitely his notes.

dialogue.speaker: Jonah
dialogue.text: Then why don't we talk to him first? He might admit it himself.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay, but if he doesn't, I think we should tell the teacher.

dialogue.speaker: Jonah
dialogue.text: That's fair. Let's find him after class and give him until tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And if he refuses, we'll go to Ms. Grant together.

titleEn: Persuading a friend to see a doctor
titleTh: เกลี้ยกล่อมเพื่อนให้ไปหาหมอ
scenarioSentences: Your friend Kai has had headaches for weeks.
He takes painkillers almost every day.
He says he is just stressed.
You are worried it is something serious.
You bring it up over dinner.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Kai, are your headaches any better?

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: Not really. But it's just stress from work. It'll pass.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's been three weeks, and you're taking painkillers every day. That's not normal.

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: I know, but I can't take time off for a doctor right now.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The clinic near your office opens at eight. You'd only miss an hour.

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: Maybe. But what if they just tell me to rest?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then at least you'd know it's nothing serious. Otherwise, you'll keep worrying.

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: That's true. My eyes have been blurry too, actually.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then you really should go. Could you book an appointment now?

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: Okay, you're right. I'll call and try to get one for tomorrow morning.

titleEn: Changing a lease when a roommate leaves
titleTh: แก้สัญญาเช่าเมื่อรูมเมตย้ายออก
scenarioSentences: You share a two-bedroom apartment with Nina.
Nina is moving out next month.
You can't pay the full rent alone.
Ms. Pryor manages the lease for the owner.
You call her for advice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Pryor, Nina is moving out, but our lease runs until June.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pryor
dialogue.text: Both names are on the lease, so you're both responsible for the rent.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I can't afford it alone, though.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pryor
dialogue.text: Could you find someone to replace her? The owner would need to approve them.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, a coworker might be interested. How long would I have?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pryor
dialogue.text: One month. Until then, Nina is still responsible for her half.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And if I can't find anyone by then?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pryor
dialogue.text: Then you could move to a one-bedroom unit, but there'd be a fee.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd rather avoid that. I'll talk to my coworker this week.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Pryor
dialogue.text: Good. Send me her details, and I'll start the paperwork.
